Executive Summary

  • Interest rate tightening: A net 43.8% of Slovak firms reported higher bank loan interest rates, rising 38.3 pp from a net 5.5% in the prior wave — the largest swing across all three geographies.
  • Margin squeeze: Labour costs rose for a net 78.81% of Slovak firms, 19.85 pp above the EA, while profits fell for a net 34.38% and turnover still contracted — cost pressures hitting weak revenues.
  • Credit line stress persists: The Slovak credit line gap held at +15.3pp, the most stressed instrument, as rising need outweighed near-flat availability even as bank loan availability improved.
  • Turnover outlook diverges: A net 6.75% of Slovak firms expected turnover to rise, down 14.15 pp from two quarters earlier and 19.1 pp below the euro area's net 25.88%.

Financing Conditions

Slovak interest rate tightening rose sharply, reaching a net 43.8% in wave 39

Changes in Terms and Conditions of Bank Financing (Q10)

  • A net 43.8% of Slovak firms (n=76) reported higher interest rates in wave 39, rising 38.3 pp from a net 5.5% in wave 38 — the largest swing across all three geographies, signalling sharply higher financing costs.
  • Available loan or credit line size tightened for a net 12.4% of Slovak firms (n=74), up 6.3 pp from wave 38, with loan maturity conditions also tightening at a net 11.6% (n=76) — squeezing liquidity buffers.
  • Euro area interest rate tightening also intensified, with a net 40.0% of firms (n=1,906) reporting higher rates, up 12.7 pp from wave 38, leaving Slovakia 3.8 pp above the EA — widening the regional cost gap.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

ⓘ SQL — bank_loan_terms.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Chart 1: Changes in terms and conditions of bank financing (Q10)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Austria (AT), Germany (DE)
-- All firm sizes combined (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves
--
-- net_balance_wtd: positive = net tightening (adverse for firms)
--                 negative = net easing (favourable for firms)
-- Sub-items:
--   a = Level of interest rates
--   b = Non-interest financing costs (charges, fees, commissions)
--   c = Available size of loan or credit line
--   d = Available maturity of the loan
--   e = Collateral requirements
--   f = Other terms (guarantees, covenants, procedures)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q10'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improved_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorated_wtd,
    f.pct_unchanged_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions f
WHERE f.question_id = 'q10'
  AND f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Credit line stress persists despite easing Slovak bank loan conditions

Financing Need vs Availability Gap (Q5/Q9)

  • The Slovak credit line gap held at +15.3pp (n=270), 1.3pp above the EA, as rising need (+15.2pp) outweighed near-flat availability (-0.1pp) — the most stressed instrument for Slovak firms.
  • The bank loan gap deepened to -6.0pp (n=214) from -4.0pp in the prior wave, 8.8pp below the EA's +2.8pp, as availability improved to +5.6pp — signalling tighter conditions for Slovak firms.
  • The trade credit gap improved by 8.0pp to -1.7pp (n=180), driven by a sharp fall in need from +7.1pp to -3.4pp, leaving SK 12.7pp less stressed than the EA.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

ⓘ SQL — financing_gap.sql (cited column: financing_gap_wtd)
-- Financing need vs availability gap (Q5/Q9) from mart_safe__financing_conditions
-- financing_gap_wtd = Q5 net balance (need) minus Q9 net balance (availability)
-- Positive gap = need exceeds availability (adverse for firms)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- Returns two result sets unioned:
--   type='main'  — bank loans (sub_item='a') for SK/EA/DE — used for the main grouped-bar chart
--   type='sk_all' — all major instruments for SK only — used for the SK instrument breakdown chart

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q9'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
),

q5 AS (
    SELECT wave_number, survey_period_label, country_code, sub_item, sub_item_label,
           net_balance_wtd AS need_nb, n_respondents AS n_respondents_need
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q5'
      AND country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
      AND firm_size = 'all'
      AND wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
),

q9 AS (
    SELECT wave_number, country_code, sub_item,
           net_balance_wtd        AS availability_nb,
           financing_gap_wtd,
           n_respondents          AS n_respondents_avail
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_conditions
    WHERE question_id = 'q9'
      AND country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
      AND firm_size = 'all'
      AND wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
),

joined AS (
    SELECT
        q5.wave_number,
        q5.survey_period_label,
        q5.country_code,
        q5.sub_item,
        q5.sub_item_label,
        q5.need_nb,
        q9.availability_nb,
        q9.financing_gap_wtd,
        q5.n_respondents_need,
        q9.n_respondents_avail
    FROM q5
    JOIN q9 USING (wave_number, country_code, sub_item)
)

-- Main chart: bank loans (a), credit lines (f), trade credit (b) for SK/EA/DE
SELECT *, 'main' AS chart_type
FROM joined
WHERE sub_item IN ('a', 'f', 'b')

UNION ALL

-- SK instrument breakdown: all instruments for Slovakia only
SELECT *, 'sk_all' AS chart_type
FROM joined
WHERE country_code = 'SK'
  AND sub_item IN ('a', 'b', 'f', 'g', 'h')

ORDER BY chart_type, sub_item, country_code, wave_number

Slovak firms' bank loan availability expectations diverged from improving EA trend

Expected Availability of External Financing (Q23)

  • A net 6.5% of Slovak firms (n=104) expected bank loan availability to deteriorate in wave 39—suggesting tightening conditions ahead for local borrowers.
  • Slovak firms' trade credit expectations improved 4.0 pp to a net 6.2% expecting deterioration (n=90), while EA firms saw only a 1.0 pp rise to 1.9%.
  • Credit line availability expectations improved for both SK and EA firms, with Slovak firms' net deterioration share falling 3.2 pp to 3.9% (n=136)—signalling slightly better short-term liquidity prospects.

* Only firms that have used or applied for this type of financing in the past are asked this question. A lower n relative to the total sample is by design and does not indicate a data quality issue — see ECB SAFE methodology for details.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — availability_expectations.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q23: Expected availability of external financing over the next quarter
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: % expecting improvement minus % expecting deterioration
-- Positive = more firms expect availability to IMPROVE (FAVOURABLE)
-- Negative = more firms expect availability to DETERIORATE (ADVERSE)
--
-- Sub-items (matching Q5/Q9 instruments):
--   b = Bank loans
--   d = Trade credit
--   g = Credit lines and bank overdraft

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__availability_expectations
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improve_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorate_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__availability_expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms lead EA in working capital financing at 57%

Purpose of Financing (Q6A)

  • Inventory and working capital remained the dominant financing purpose for Slovak firms, cited by 57.0% (n=242) — 16.2 pp above the euro area's 40.8% — compared with 55.7% in the previous wave, underlining their heavy reliance on short-term liquidity.
  • Fixed investment financing rose from 34.2% to 40.7% among Slovak firms (n=242), a gain of 6.5 pp that brought Slovakia above the euro area rate of 38.4%, suggesting growing capacity for long-term growth investments.
  • Refinancing or paying off obligations declined from 21.5% to 17.0% among Slovak firms (n=241), narrowing the gap with the euro area's 15.8%, indicating reduced debt servicing pressure.
ⓘ SQL — financing_purpose.sql (cited column: pct_cited_wtd)
-- Q6A: Purpose of financing (multi-select)
-- pct_cited_wtd = % of firms citing each purpose (can sum > 100% as multi-select)
-- purposes: 1=Fixed investment, 2=Inventory/working capital, 3=Hiring/training,
--           4=New products/services, 5=Refinancing, 6=Other
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_purpose
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.purpose_id,
    f.purpose_label,
    f.pct_cited_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_purpose f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.purpose_id, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Bank willingness stable in Slovakia but macro outlook deteriorates further

Factors Affecting Access to External Financing (Q11)

  • A net 7.8% of Slovak firms (n=310) reported that banks' willingness to provide credit improved, unchanged from the previous wave and above the EA's net 5.6% and Germany's net -4.2% — suggesting stable financing conditions.
  • A net 51.6% of Slovak firms (n=472) reported a deteriorating general economic outlook, worsening by 7.2 pp from wave 38, and 22.2 pp more negative than the EA's net 29.4% — putting pressure on future investment plans.
  • Access to public financial support remained negative for Slovak firms (n=310) at a net -21.2%, though notably less so than wave 38's net -33.8%, compared with the EA's net -13.6% — limiting mitigation options for firms.
ⓘ SQL — financing_factors.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q11: Self-assessed factors affecting availability of external financing
-- Net balance = % reporting improvement minus % reporting deterioration
-- Positive = factor improving (favourable for financing access)
-- Negative = factor deteriorating (adverse / potential credit supply constraint)
--
-- Key sub-items for credit supply analysis:
--   f = Willingness of banks to provide credit  (direct bank supply signal)
--   a = General economic outlook                (macro drag on supply)
--   b = Access to public financial support      (policy/guarantee channel)
--
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_factors
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.pct_improved_wtd,
    f.pct_deteriorated_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__financing_factors f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.sub_item IN ('f', 'a', 'b')
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Economic Situation of Firms

Slovak turnover still contracting despite 13 pp improvement in wave 39

Business Situation Indicators (Q2)

  • A net 12.83% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported declining turnover in wave 39, improving 13.39 pp from a net 26.22% decline in wave 38 — yet still signalling weak demand conditions.
  • A net 34.38% of Slovak firms (n=242) reported falling profits — 18.99 pp worse than the EA's net 15.39% — highlighting profitability pressures.
  • Labour costs continued to rise for a net 78.81% of Slovak firms (n=242), 19.85 pp above the EA's net 58.96% — squeezing margins further.
ⓘ SQL — business_situation.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q2: Business situation indicators (turnover, labour costs, profit, investment, employees)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- sub_items: a=Turnover, b=Labour costs, e=Profit, g=Investment, i=Employees
-- Sign: positive = indicator rising; labour costs positive = costs rising (adverse)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_situation
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,
    f.sub_item_label,

    f.pct_decreased_wtd,

FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_situation f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak turnover expectations fell sharply while EA firms remained optimistic

Expected Changes in Turnover and Investment (Q26)

  • A net 6.75% of Slovak firms (n=228) expected turnover to increase over the next two quarters, down 14.15 pp from two quarters earlier, against a net 25.88% for the euro area (n=5,266) — signalling weaker domestic demand.
  • Slovak fixed investment expectations rose to a net 14.67% (n=228), up 3.88 pp from two quarters earlier, outpacing the euro area's net 9.45% and Germany's net -2.42% — suggesting some firms are betting on future growth despite current headwinds.
  • The 19.1 pp gap between Slovak and euro area turnover expectations points to diverging near-term growth trajectories, with Slovak firms' revenue outlook the weakest among the three economies compared.

‡ This question is not fielded every quarter — consecutive points on this chart may be more than one quarter apart. See point labels for the actual survey period.

ⓘ SQL — outlook.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q26: Expected changes in turnover and investments over the next two quarters
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: positive = more firms expect increase (FAVOURABLE)
--                 negative = more firms expect decrease (ADVERSE)
-- Sub-items:
--   a = Company's turnover
--   b = Investments in property, plant or equipment

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__outlook
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.sub_item,

WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'

Slovak firms face margin compression as input costs outpace selling prices

Price, Wage and Employment Expectations (Q31/Q34)

  • Slovak firms (n=224) expected production input prices to rise 7.33% over the next 12 months, far exceeding selling price expectations of 3.75% (n=222), pointing to sustained margin compression.
  • Slovak wage expectations held at 4.12% (n=233), easing only 0.09 pp from wave 38, and ran 1.52 pp above the euro area's 2.60%, reinforcing the cost-side squeeze.
  • Five-year inflation expectations among Slovak firms stood at 7.66% (n=165), declining 0.91 pp from wave 38 but remaining 1.72 pp above the EA average of 5.94%.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — expectations_quantitative.sql (cited column: mean_wtd)
-- Q31/Q34: Quantitative expectations — inflation rate (Q31) and expected % changes
-- in selling prices, input costs, wages, employment (Q34).
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- mean_wtd: weighted mean expected % change (NOT a net balance)
-- Positive = firms expect an increase; negative = firms expect a decrease.
--
-- Sub-items:
--   Q31_a = Expected inflation rate in 12 months
--   Q34_a = Average selling price of products/services
--   Q34_b = Average prices of production inputs (non-labour)
--   Q34_c = Average wage of employees
--   Q34_d = Number of employees
--
-- panel_id = question_id || '_' || sub_item to disambiguate Q31/Q34 sub_item 'a'

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations
    WHERE question_id = 'q34'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.question_id,
    f.sub_item,
    f.question_id || '_' || f.sub_item                          AS panel_id,
    f.sub_item_label,
    f.mean_wtd,
    f.p25_unwtd,
    f.median_unwtd,
    f.p75_unwtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.question_id IN ('q31', 'q34')
  AND f.sub_item IN ('a', 'b', 'c', 'd')
  AND f.mean_wtd IS NOT NULL
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.question_id, f.sub_item, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Slovak firms' upside inflation risk balance diverges further from euro area

Inflation Risk Outlook (Q33)

  • A net 61.2% of Slovak firms (n=242) saw upside risks to five-year inflation, rising 2.3 pp from net 58.9% in wave 38, while the EA balance eased to net 54.0% (n=5,087) — suggesting growing divergence in inflation expectations.
  • The SK–EA gap widened to 7.2 pp as Slovak firms' upside risk balance rose and the euro area's declined by 1.3 pp — indicating increasing local inflation concerns.
  • Upside inflation risk remained the dominant view across all three economies, with net balances well above zero for Slovakia, the euro area, and Germany.

† Observations with fewer than 10 valid responses in a given wave × country × sub-item cell are excluded from the chart; gaps in series indicate insufficient data for that period.

ⓘ SQL — expectations_risk.sql (cited column: net_balance_wtd)
-- Q33: Main risk to 5-year inflation outlook (ordinal net balance)
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)
--
-- net_balance_wtd: % seeing upside inflation risk minus % seeing downside risk
-- Positive = more firms see inflation as a risk to the upside
-- Negative = more firms see inflation risk to the downside

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations
    WHERE question_id = 'q33'
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.pct_downside_wtd,
    f.pct_balanced_wtd,
    f.pct_upside_wtd,
    f.net_balance_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__expectations f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.question_id = 'q33'
  AND f.n_respondents >= 10
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.country_code, f.wave_number

Skilled staff shortage tops Slovak business concerns in Wave 39

Most Pressing Business Problems (Q0B)

  • Skilled staff availability ranked as the most pressing problem among the seven tested for Slovak firms (n=239), scoring 6.64/10 — up from 6.07 in the previous wave, exceeding the EA's 6.57, signalling rising operational strain.
  • Costs of production or labour scored 6.62/10 (n=240), rising from 6.19 in the previous wave, though remaining below the EA average of 6.74 — highlighting cost pressures without yet matching peers.
  • Regulation scored 6.10/10 (n=236), easing 0.08 from the previous wave, yet still above the EA's 5.87 — suggesting persistent compliance burdens for Slovak firms.
ⓘ SQL — business_problems.sql (cited column: avg_pressingness_wtd)
-- Q0B: Most pressing business problems
-- Countries: Slovakia (SK), Euro Area (EA), Germany (DE)
-- All firms (firm_size = 'all'), last 4 waves (dynamic)

WITH latest_waves AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT wave_number
    FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_problems
    ORDER BY wave_number DESC
    LIMIT 4
)

SELECT
    f.wave_number,
    f.survey_period_label,
    f.country_code,
    f.problem_id,
    f.problem_label,
    f.avg_pressingness_wtd,
    f.n_respondents
FROM main_safe.mart_safe__business_problems f
WHERE f.country_code IN ('SK', 'EA', 'DE')
  AND f.firm_size = 'all'
  AND f.wave_number IN (SELECT wave_number FROM latest_waves)
ORDER BY f.problem_id, f.country_code, f.wave_number

Source: ECB SAFE microdata. Net balance = % reporting increase minus % reporting decrease. Positive = tightening/rising (adverse for firms unless noted). Negative = easing/falling.
